answer: The raven multiplier is published, charged in anchor, and willow lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3336 identities would post 2082 proofs and burn roughly 59 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
